newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cemig shrs jump again on rumors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cemig shrs jump again on rumors.

text.p: Common shares of Brazilian power firm Cemig surged for a second consecutive day on rumors a Chilean firm will buy a third of the company's voting stock, traders said.

Common shares of state-owned Cemig had shot up 10.4 percent to 48.00 reais, a rise of 4.50 reais from Thursday's close, by 1324 local time/1224 EDT on the Sao Paulo bourse. The stock had traded as high as 49.50 reais, a 13.8 percent rise, before dropping back some.
"It's the same rumors as yesterday, that a Chilean firm has bought 30 percent of the ordinary shares," a broker told Reuters.

Minas Gerais state plans to auction a 33 percent stake in Cemig at a December auction. Four foreign firms -- Southern Electric, France's EDF, Canada's Hydro Quebec and Chile's Chilectra -- have expressed interest in bidding on the shares, a company official said.

Governor Eduardo Azevedo travelled to Santiago this week on an official visit to drum up investor interest in his state. Among other activities, he was expected to make a visit to Chilectra. The market talk has not named a specific Chilean company.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was up 0.44 percent at 66,557 points at 1330 local time/1230 EDT.

Cemig common led a general rise in power shares, including blue-chip Eletrobras, which was up 1.89 percent or 5.99 reais at 322.99 reais, and Sao Paulo state's CPFL, up 1.05 percent or 1.00 real at 95.00 reais.
